one_line: Sonar's SonarQube Hunter Agent: an on-demand/scheduled AI security agent that maps a repo, runs three specialized issue-class agents with adversarial validation and noise gates, and surfaces logic/authz flaws (IDOR, broken access control, business logic, auth/session) in SonarQube's normal issue list.
summary: Taylor Luttrell-Williams of Sonar demos SonarQube Hunter Agent, an AI security agent aimed at logic-level vulnerabilities that pattern-based SAST misses. The pipeline first maps the repository globally, then runs three specialized agents, one per issue class, followed by adversarial validation and noise gates to cut false positives. Findings are deduplicated and exported into SonarQube's existing issue list with severity, location, explanation and fix guidance. In the demo, a scan of a small Python app took about an hour and produced 46 open issues across broken access control, business logic and authentication/session categories. The talk is a product walkthrough and sponsor pitch: it announces Sonar joining the OpenAI Daybreak Cyber Partner Program for frontier security models and says automatic remediation via a remediation agent is newly available. It gives no independent benchmark or precision/recall numbers, so the detection quality claims are unverified.

key_ideas.idea: SAST is pattern-based and misses intent-level flaws; code can be functionally correct yet violate business logic or authorization intent.
key_ideas.detail: Speaker frames a new class of agent as needed because agent-generated code ships fast and pen tests happen only a few times a year.

key_ideas.idea: Architecture is a global repo map, then three specialized agents, one per issue class, followed by adversarial validation and noise gates.
key_ideas.detail: The map is used to derive security expectations from component relationships. Adversarial validation is meant to remove false positives, and noise gates drop low-validity or by-design findings.

key_ideas.idea: Findings are merged into the existing SonarQube issue list rather than a separate dashboard.
key_ideas.detail: Issues carry a Hunter Agent tag and a class tag, get a severity, point to the exact code location, and can be assigned, accepted, confirmed or marked false positive, like any other Sonar issue.

key_ideas.idea: Recommended setup is layered: keep SAST and SCA running and add Hunter Agent on top of them in one platform.
key_ideas.detail: The speaker frames this as two independent verification layers (zero-trust, defense in depth), not a replacement for SAST.

key_ideas.idea: Scans are slow and whole-codebase; expect roughly an hour for a project.
key_ideas.detail: On-demand Scan Now shows an estimated number of units before running. Scheduled scans can run daily, weekly or monthly, on a chosen branch. Works with SonarQube Cloud or self-hosted SonarQube Server.

key_ideas.idea: Scan pipeline steps: clone repo, map attack surface and build a threat model, run contextual scans, dedupe findings from sub-agents, export validated issues.
key_ideas.detail: Categories shown in the demo: broken access control (IDOR, missing authz, privilege escalation, sensitive data exposure, CSRF), business logic (skipped workflow steps, abusable repeatable actions, missing rate limits), and authentication/session (session fixation, non-expiring sessions, weak password recovery, missing MFA, brute force).

key_ideas.idea: Business-logic issues can now be auto-remediated by a SonarQube remediation agent, which can also run on a schedule.
key_ideas.detail: Speaker says this became available the week of the talk. This is an announcement from the talk, not a verified feature. Demo did not show it running.

techniques.name: Multi-agent security scan with validation gates
techniques.how: 1) Global repo map. 2) Derive security expectations from component relationships. 3) Run three class-specialized agents in parallel (broken access control, business logic, auth/session). 4) Adversarial validation pass to reject false positives. 5) Noise gate to drop low-validity or by-design issues. 6) Dedupe and merge into a single issue list with severity and file location.
techniques.when: When pattern-based SAST cannot catch intent or authorization flaws, and code ships faster than pen tests run.

techniques.name: Layered verification: SAST plus logic-level agent
techniques.how: Keep SAST and SCA as the deterministic layer, and add an AI logic-bug agent as a second, independent layer in the same platform, so each finding source covers the other's blind spots.
techniques.when: When you want defense in depth and cannot rely on a single scanner to catch everything.

techniques.name: Triage workflow for AI-raised issues
techniques.how: Triage each issue as accept (valid but non-blocking, does not affect the quality gate), confirm (valid and blocks the gate), or false positive. Assign to a developer. Scheduled scans let you re-run on a branch at a chosen cadence.
techniques.when: When you need to route AI-generated security findings through an existing issue-tracking and quality-gate process.

tools: OpenAI Daybreak Cyber Partner Program (frontier cybersecurity models)

numbers.claim: Scan duration: about one hour for the demo project; can take longer on large or complex codebases ('upwards of an hour').
Demo output: 46 open issues across three categories (broken access control, business logic, authentication/session); 5 business-logic findings noted.
Pen tests typically happen at most twice per year, or about once per quarter, per the speaker's framing.

hot_takes: Vendor pitch: the talk is a product demo with an Daybreak/OpenAI partnership announcement and a just-released auto-remediation feature. It gives no independent precision or recall numbers, so the detection claims are unverified.
The speaker frames SAST as insufficient and Hunter Agent as the fix for logic bugs, but also recommends running both together. The message is complementary, not replacement.

Validation is claimed to reduce false positives via adversarial checks, but the talk gives no false-positive rate. The demo only showed one high-severity access-control finding and one MFA-bypass finding in detail.

relevance.why: Sits in the L2C Crucible / exec-gate and security-guardrails space. Its multi-stage pattern (global map, class-specialized agents, adversarial validation, noise gates, dedupe) is a reusable review design for agent-written code.
relevance.action: Read the adversarial-validation and noise-gate design, then consider a validation pass that rejects false positives before findings reach any reviewer or gate.

relevance.why: ProsHarness runs Claude Code agents in long unattended loops and schedules. A scheduled, multi-agent security review with a validation gate fits its plan-critique-debate pattern.
relevance.action: Add an optional post-run security review step that runs a Hunter-style class-split pass plus adversarial validation over changes an agent produced, and gates on validated findings only.
